predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: ratio of the RL/base hold-on rate ratio far from the last numeric result to the same ratio near it, R(d >= 1500) / R(d < 200), on finished MATH-500 answers. The constant-bias rival (r4-m06) predicts about 1.0; the wrap-up-replacement rival predicts below 1.0; this mechanism predicts well above 1.
predictions.recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue) and runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain), from inventory.md (readable now). Keep rows with cap_hit false; rows missing or with empty text contribute nothing. In each text replace every match of the regex (?<=\d),(?=\d{3}) by '' (commas between digits deleted). Result positions: for each match of '=\s*-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?' the index just after the match end; for each occurrence of '\boxed{' the index just after its brace-balanced closing '}' (skip a box that is unbalanced before the end of text). For each character index i in [0, len(text)), d(i) = i - r* where r* is the largest result position <= i; if no result position is <= i, d(i) = i. Bins of d: B1 [0,200), B2 [200,600), B3 [600,1500), B4 [1500, inf). Exposure of a bin = number of character indices with d in the bin, summed over all kept rows of a model. Events = start indices of matches of the case-sensitive regex (?<![A-Za-z])(Wait|Hmm)(?![A-Za-z]); each event is binned by d at its start index. rate_b = 1000 * events_b / exposure_b per model; R_b = rate_b(RL) / rate_b(base). Statistic = R_4 / R_1. If any base rate in B1 or B4 is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Files: runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue; 500 rows, 27 cap_hit true) and runs/theory-rows/s3k/r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain; 500 rows, 6 cap_hit true), the paths the recipe names; if absent the script fetches them from S3 (inventory.md commands) into runs/theory-tests/. Kept: cap_hit is False and non-empty text; one row per problem_index (sample is 0 everywhere). Exposure and events are pooled over all kept rows of each model (unpaired), as the recipe says 'summed over all kept rows of a model'. alt_measured: same statistic on the problems where both models have a kept row (paired reading). Brace balancing counts every '{' and '}' literally, including escaped \{ \}; a box result position equal to len(text) adds no exposure. Duplicate result positions are merged. The stored texts start with the tail of the prompt (e.g. ' line!' or ' tag.'); the text field is used as is, without stripping it. d(i) before the first result is i, so the opening of every answer counts in B1/B2 before any result has been stated, which mixes 'right after a result' with 'start of the answer'. Bootstrap over problems (union of problem indices) with pooled ratios recomputed per resample; an undefined resample is sorted as -inf. n = number of problems with at least one kept row.

predictions.experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: the RL/base hold-on rate ratio within 200 characters after a stated numeric result (bin B1 alone). The overall written ratio is about 1.4 (result-8695c6, 8.81 vs 6.24 per 1,000 tokens), which a reader without the theory would expect here too; the timer says the excess is near zero right after a result.
predictions.recipe: Same files, filters, comma deletion, result positions, d(i), events and exposure as the first prediction. Statistic = R_1 = (1000 * events in B1 / exposure in B1 for T2) / (1000 * events in B1 / exposure in B1 for T1). Cap-hit rows excluded; missing rows contribute nothing; if the T1 rate in B1 is 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: statistic above 1.3 or below 0.75, or undefined
predictions.note: Same files, filters, result positions, d(i), events and exposure as k=1. Statistic R_1 = (1000*events_B1/exposure_B1 for T2) / (same for T1), pooled over all kept rows of each model. Undefined (refuted_without_number) only if the T1 B1 rate is 0 (or a B1 exposure is 0); a T2 B1 rate of 0 gives R_1 = 0, which is defined and refuted (< 0.75). alt_measured: paired reading (problems where both models have a kept row). B1 includes the first 200 characters of every answer (d = i before any result), not only positions right after a stated result; this could raise or lower R_1 relative to the theory's intended 'right after a result' reading. Undefined bootstrap resamples (practically impossible) are sorted as +inf.

predictions.experiment: Cause test against a position rival: the same far/near contrast R(d >= 1500) / R(d < 200), computed only on character positions in the first half of each answer. The rival in which RL's excess comes from a late verification phase of the answer (excess grows with position in the answer, not with distance from a result) predicts about 1.0 here; the timer, which resets at every result regardless of where it is, predicts a clearly rising profile in the first half as well.
predictions.recipe: Same files, filters, comma deletion, result positions, d(i) (computed on the full text), bins and event regex as the first prediction, but count exposure only for character indices i < len(text) / 2 (len of the comma-deleted text) and count only events whose start index s < len(text) / 2. Per model and bin, rate_b = 1000 * events_b / exposure_b; R_b = rate_b(T2) / rate_b(T1). Statistic = R_4 / R_1. Cap hits excluded, missing rows contribute nothing; if any T1 rate in B1 or B4 is 0, or any T2 exposure in B4 is 0, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Same as k=1 but exposure counts only indices i < len(text)/2 (integer i < ceil(L/2), L = length of the comma-deleted text) and only events whose start index is < len(text)/2; d(i) and result positions are computed on the full comma-deleted text (results in the second half cannot affect first-half indices anyway). Undefined (refuted_without_number) if a T1 rate in B1 or B4 is 0, T2 exposure in B4 is 0, or the T2 B1 rate is 0 (R_1 = 0 makes R_4/R_1 undefined). alt_measured: paired reading (problems where both models have a kept row). B4 exposure in the first half needs answers with 1500+ result-free characters early on, so B4 may be thin and the ratio noisy; B1 again includes each answer's opening 200 characters.
